{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SuD2EBWYkzcXvmTkBP27gC","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/bin/sh\n# run.sh — LayersTesting grader. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Exercises ./ledger against a fresh database and compares every command's exit code and standard\n# output with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/LayersTesting/bin/run.sh APP  from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a\n# SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory. Every run starts with `ledger init`, so the grader\n# never depends on prior state. Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/seed_accounts.csv\" ]; then SEED=$HERE; else SEED=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nLEDGER=\"$APP/ledger\"\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nDATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-$WORK/ledger.db}\nexport DATABASE_URL\n\nif [ ! -x \"$LEDGER\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./ledger at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <ledger args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$LEDGER\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: ledger $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: ledger $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. Schema lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck A1 0 init < /dev/null\ncheck A2 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,0\ncategories,0\ntransactions,0\nEOF\n\n# ── B. Bulk load of the known dataset ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck B1 0 load accounts \"$SEED/seed_accounts.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\naccounts,4\nEOF\ncheck B2 0 load categories \"$SEED/seed_categories.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ncategories,7\nEOF\ncheck B3 0 load transactions \"$SEED/seed_transactions.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ntransactions,120\nEOF\ncheck B4 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,4\ncategories,7\ntransactions,120\nEOF\n\n# ── C. Reports over the seeded rows ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck C1 0 report balances <<'EOF'\naccount,name,transactions,balance\nDRAWER1,Front Drawer,39,2299.38\nDRAWER2,Back Drawer,39,1378.32\nPETTY,Petty Cash,21,306.25\nSAFE,Store Safe,21,250.00\nTOTAL,,120,4233.95\nEOF\ncheck C2 0 report categories <<'EOF'\ncategory,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net\nOPENING,Opening balance,2,5200.00,0.00,5200.00\nPAYROLL,Payroll,6,0.00,7200.00,-7200.00\nREFUND,Customer refunds,12,0.00,101.25,-101.25\nRENT,Rent,3,0.00,2700.00,-2700.00\nSALES,Sales receipts,64,9578.95,0.00,9578.95\nSUPPLY,Supplies,15,0.00,543.75,-543.75\nTRANSFER,Internal transfer,18,5100.00,5100.00,0.00\nTOTAL,,120,19878.95,15645.00,4233.95\nEOF\ncheck C3 0 report monthly <<'EOF'\nmonth,transactions,inflow,outflow,net\n2026-01,40,9659.45,5215.00,4444.45\n2026-02,40,4979.65,5215.00,-235.35\n2026-03,40,5239.85,5215.00,24.85\nTOTAL,120,19878.95,15645.00,4233.95\nEOF\n\n# ── D. A rejected load changes nothing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck D1 3 load transactions \"$SEED/seed_transactions_bad.csv\" < /dev/null\ncheck D2 3 load accounts \"$SEED/seed_accounts.csv\" < /dev/null\ncheck D3 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,4\ncategories,7\ntransactions,120\nEOF\n\n# ── E. Account create, read, update, delete ──────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck E1 0 account add CASH9 \"Event Float\" <<'EOF'\naccount,name,transactions,balance\nCASH9,Event Float,0,0.00\nEOF\ncheck E2 3 account add CASH9 \"Event Float\" < /dev/null\ncheck E3 0 account get CASH9 <<'EOF'\naccount,name,transactions,balance\nCASH9,Event Float,0,0.00\nEOF\ncheck E4 0 account rename CASH9 \"Event Cash Box\" <<'EOF'\naccount,name,transactions,balance\nCASH9,Event Cash Box,0,0.00\nEOF\ncheck E5 4 account get NOSUCH < /dev/null\ncheck E6 3 account delete DRAWER1 < /dev/null\ncheck E7 0 account delete CASH9 <<'EOF'\ndeleted\nCASH9\nEOF\ncheck E8 4 account get CASH9 < /dev/null\n\n# ── F. Transaction create, read, update, delete ──────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck F1 0 txn post DRAWER1 SALES 45.50 2026-04-01 \"walk in sale\" <<'EOF'\ntxn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo\n121,2026-04-01,DRAWER1,SALES,45.50,walk in sale\nEOF\ncheck F2 0 txn get 121 <<'EOF'\ntxn_id,date,account,category,amount,memo\n121,2026-04-01,DRAWER1,SALES,45.50,walk in sale\nEOF","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ecc0238a-9bf0-4ee3-bb57-3ad8e5319b5f","uuid":"2ab34613-40f0-4072-8e4a-fcc0b056e566","timestamp":"2026-10-25T17:05:08.434Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/bin/sh\n# run.sh — LayersTesting grader. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input fields; each is compared with its declared column, else its own.\"\"\"\n        by_field = {field: (op, column) for field, op, column in compare}\n        terms = []\n        for offset, name in f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n and PostgreSQL spell the statement identically.\n        \"\"\"\n        assigned = [name for name in columns if name not in match]\n        target = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in match)\n NOTHING\"\n        )\n        return f\"{self.insert(table, columns, None)} ON CONFLICT ({target}) {action}\"\n\n    def delete(\n        self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str], compare: compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n sign, whole, fraction = match.groups()\n    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or \"\").ljust(2, \"0\"))\n    if cents == 0:\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must not be zero\")\n    return \"\"\"Return ``text`` if it is a real calendar date written as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    match = _DATE.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"date must look like
